scripts.//dev: --kill-others: closing either half must take the other with it — without it the survivor (usually Vite) lingers invisibly and squats its port for the next start.
scripts.//dev:backend: 8734 on purpose — the port Vite's proxy targets AND the desktop shell prefers: a shell launched while this runs ADOPTS this backend instead of starting the jar, so devtools hot-restarts (triggered by the IDE compiling on save, or `mvn compile`) reach the real app. Java edits reload in seconds; only a dependency change still needs a restart. --server.address matches what the desktop profile sets, and is not merely cosmetic: without it Tomcat binds every interface, which pops the Windows Firewall dialog on the first run after any JDK change AND leaves a dev backend — with authentication off — reachable from the network.
scripts.//desktop:build: -DskipTests: this is the launch-the-app loop, and paying the full suite on every UI tweak makes people stop launching the app. CI runs the tests on every push; `pnpm backend:build` still runs them for a deliberate pre-release check.
scripts.desktop:build: pnpm --filter frontend build && cd apps/backend && mvn -q clean package -DskipTests
scripts.//desktop:dev: The live loop INSIDE the real app: Vite serves the UI with hot reload, the Electron shell detects it and loads it instead of the jar's baked copy, and Vite proxies /api and /ws to the backend (8734). Frontend edits appear on save. For backend hot reload too, start `pnpm dev:backend` FIRST: the shell adopts it and Spring devtools restarts it on every recompile — no jar rebuild. Without it the shell runs the last jar from target/, so build that once first.
scripts.desktop:dev: concurrently --kill-others -n ui,shell -c green,magenta "pnpm dev:frontend" "pnpm --filter desktop start"
